confirmed.title: Regression: the new percent-encoded separators (%3a, %3d) end a key match on a word character, so a secret key right after one is never read. Text that 2ec0bba and 7193877 both masked now shows its secret
confirmed.fix:
Let a key start right after a percent-encoded quote or separator:
`(?:(?<![\w.-])|(?<=%(?:2[27]|3[ad])))(?<!\\(?=\\))${QUOTE}?…`
The lookbehind is constant-time. With it (fix/ in my dir):
- the four shapes are masked;
- 4a284f9's 65 data-diff tests pass;
- 150K fuzz cases over 4 seeds, plus the corpus, give 0 regressions against 7193877.
Add a test with `x%3dpassword=…` and `value%3a…--db-token=`.

votes.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. I reproduced it with my own probe on a fresh clone. The head is 4a284f9, and `git diff --name-status 561bd84..HEAD` lists only #35's files: CHANGELOG.md, README.md, lib/data-diff.mjs, package.json and test/data-diff.test.mjs.

**Probe (probe.mjs, field `note`, columns 2ec0bba / 7193877 / 4a284f9).** I ran sanitizeSnapshot with no rules on each of the three engine versions:
- `x%3dpassword=Zq9SeCr3tVal`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `x%3Apassword: Zq9SeCr3tVal`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `value%3aZq9SeCr3tVal--db-token=`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `state%3AZq9SeCr3tValtoken%22%3dtoken:`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `next=x%3Dpassword=Zq9SeCr3tVal`: masked / masked / CLEAR. This is a more realistic shape, a query value that is only partly encoded.
- `x%3dapi_key=…` and `x%3dtoken=…`: masked / masked / CLEAR

Controls with a plain separator still mask on all heads: `x=password=…`, `x:password: …` and `x=1 password=…`. `a%3D1&password=…` also still masks.

**Mechanism (lib/data-diff.mjs:349).** KEY_IN_TEXT now ends a match with `(?:[:=]|%3[ad])`, using flags `gi`. A short key before the escape, such as `x`, is matched and its match consumes `%3d`. The scan then resumes at `password`, whose preceding character `d` fails `(?<![\w.-])`, and every later start inside the word fails the same way. In 7193877 the escape was never consumed. The scan found the key `3dpassword` starting after `%`, and SECRET_NAME matched `pass` in it.

This contradicts the README line 413 promise that a key counts at a word's start, "quoted or not … or their percent-encodings". So the round-4 change undid masking that both earlier heads gave.

**Fuzz (fuzz.mjs, 30K cases from a percent-heavy alphabet, my own seed).** Against 7193877 there were 57 regressions at 4a284f9 and 0 with the proposed fix. All 57 are this class: some key, possibly closed by a quote such as `Zq9"%3Dapi_key:`, eats an encoded `=` or `:`, and a secret key follows with no `&`, `%26` or space in between.

**Proposed fix.** I applied `(?:(?<![\w.-])|(?<=%(?:2[27]|3[ad])))` in place of `(?<![\w.-])` in a copy (fix/). It masks every shape above. It also masks two shapes that no head masked: `a%3Dpassword%3D…` and `q=a%3dpassword%3d…`. 4a284f9's own 65 data-diff tests pass with it (`node --test --test-force-exit`). The existing percent test (line 1363, `q=1&password%3D…`) has `&` before the key, so it never covers this shape.

**Severity.** The trigger needs partial or mixed encoding, so the shape is narrow. But it is a secret value shown in clear that both earlier heads masked. That falls squarely in the owner's blocking class "a regression of something previously masked", so high stands.

**Cleanup.** No node processes from this run are still running.

I could not refute this claim. The head is 4a284f9 and `git diff --name-status 561bd84..HEAD` lists only #35's own files (CHANGELOG.md, README.md, lib/data-diff.mjs, package.json, test/data-diff.test.mjs). The cause is in #35's round-4 change to KEY_IN_TEXT in lib/data-diff.mjs, so it is in scope.

**Cause.** At 7193877 the separator was `[:=]` with flag 'g'. At 4a284f9 it is `(?:[:=]|%3[ad])` with flag 'gi'.
- A match can now end on the 'd' or 'a' of '%3d' or '%3a', which are word characters.
- matchAll picks up just after that match, and `(?<![\w.-])` then fails at every character of the next key.
- So a secret key straight after an encoded separator is never read.
- Before this round the same text matched '3dpassword' (it starts after '%', which is not in `[\w.-]`), and SECRET_NAME found 'pass' in it.

**Reproduction.** probe.mjs in my dir ran `createMasker(...).cell('things', 'note', s)` against the engine file from each head. Columns below are 2ec0bba / 7193877 / 4a284f9:
- `x%3dpassword=Zq9SeCr3tVal`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `x%3Apassword: Zq9SeCr3tVal`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `value%3aZq9SeCr3tVal--db-token=abc`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `state%3AZq9SeCr3tValtoken%22%3dtoken:`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- `q=a%3Dpassword=hunter2xyz`, `a%3Dapi_key=sk_9283jfjd` and `a=b%3Dsecret=hunter2`: masked / masked / CLEAR
- Controls with a space, '&' or '%26' before the secret key stay masked at all three heads (`msg%3A password=…`, `user%3Dbob;password=…`, `next=%2Flogin%3Fuser%3Dbob%26password=…`). This confirms how narrow the shape is.

**Fuzzing.** My own fuzz.mjs used a percent-heavy token alphabet with seeds 3, 11 and 29, 40K cases each.
- 4a284f9 shows 102, 95 and 104 strings in clear that 7193877 masked.
- Every one of them has an encoded separator straight before a secret-looking key; none fall in another class.

**Proposed fix.** I applied the reviewer's start lookbehind, `(?:(?<![\w.-])|(?<=%(?:2[27]|3[ad])))`, to a copy of 4a284f9.
- It masks every case above.
- It has 0 regressions against 7193877 across the same 120K cases.
- 4a284f9's own test/data-diff.test.mjs passes 65 of 65, unchanged from the head.

The earlier masking was also partly incidental (it read the key as '3dpassword'). Even so, it is text both earlier heads masked and that now shows a secret-looking value in clear in the Data panel. confirmed.title: Regression: the tag fix `(?:\s[^<>]{0,256})?>` no longer sees a secret-named tag with a '<' in an attribute value, so text that 7193877 masked whole now shows its secret
confirmed.fix:
Don't scan attributes at all. Take a tag name followed by whitespace, '/' or '>':
`/<(?:[\w.-]{1,64}:)?([\w.-]{1,128})(?=[\s/>])/g`
Every match of 7193877's pattern is a match of this one (the name is followed by '>' or whitespace). It is linear, with no backtracking.

Measured with fix/:
- all four shapes are masked, and fuzz finds 0 regressions;
- the 65 data-diff tests pass, including the tag timing test;
- CPU on a 256 KB '<a ' cell: 33 ms, against 2.3 ms at head and 89 ms at 7193877. The test's 24 cells take 472 ms against 288 ms. Under W28=B, that cost is acceptable.

A cheaper alternative keeps head's pattern and adds closing tags (`<\/?(?:…:)?(name)…`). It keeps head's speed but still misses self-closing or unclosed tags.

Add a test with a '<' in an attribute, and update the CHANGELOG line.

- `<wsse:Password Type="a<b">…`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR / masked
- `<secret-note title="x < y">…`: CLEAR / masked / CLEAR / masked

- **Head swapped one leak for another.** 7193877 showed round 4's shape in clear (`x <a <password>…`, `cost <5 <password>…`). Head masks those, and the fix masks both classes.
- **The shape is older than 7193877.** 2ec0bba also showed these four shapes in clear, and none of this was ever on main. Still, 7193877 is the previous round's head, which this lens compares against, and its masking of tags with attributes was deliberate: its README already claimed it. **Why high.** This is a secret shown in clear and a regression against 7193877, both blocking classes. It sits at the low end of high. votes.reasoning:
I could not refute it; my own probe shows the same behaviour. Clean clone, pr35 head is 4a284f9, and `git diff --name-status 561bd84..HEAD` lists only CHANGELOG.md, README.md, lib/data-diff.mjs, package.json and test/data-diff.test.mjs. The probe (verify-adversarial-2-repro/probe.mjs, run via run.sh) runs the 7193877 engine (git show) and the 4a284f9 engine side by side. Setup: the seeded users table has fields [id, name, email], the base pane changes no schema, and the PR pane's before snapshot also has padding columns, which the click drops along with `email`.

Results, the same with trusted true and false:
- **A, 5 `aa_tmp_000N` columns.**
  - 7193877: 6 per-field red flags, one with field 'email' at index 5.
  - 4a284f9: 1 flag, `['users','column-dropped','red',shared false,count 6,fields [aa_tmp_0000..aa_tmp_0004]]`. 'email' appears nowhere in the flag list.
- **A2, 1,600 `aa_` columns.** 4a284f9 gives count 1601 and fields aa_0000..aa_0004, with no email. (At 7193877 the email flag was at index 1600, already past #37's 100-flag cap.)
- **A4, capital letters (`E0`..`E4`).** They also push email out, since uppercase sorts before lowercase. So any seeded name can be displaced with 5 well-chosen names.
- **A3, `zz_` padding.** Email is listed first.
- **A5, only 4 padding columns.** Email is still listed, so 5 is the threshold.

The data is still there:
- the PR diff's fieldsDropped is in declared order, `['email','aa_tmp_0000',…]`;
- divergence has `{kind:'field-dropped', field:'email', status:'pr-only'}`.

Cause, lib/data-diff.mjs:833: `fields: [...mine.items].sort().slice(0, 5)`. This was added by this round's fold (tally L915 replaced the per-field add), so it is in 7193877..HEAD scope. The existing test at test/data-diff.test.mjs:341-344 ("the first five by name, whatever the declared order") makes the sort deliberate. Nothing covers a seeded column dropped among 5 or more padding columns that sort first. The 1,600-column test at L1211 drops only padding.

Why it is not high:
- The flag stays red, unshared, with count 6, PR 6, base 0. Nothing is excused or turned amber.
- The drop still shows in the diff (declared order, email first) and in divergence.
- So it is not "hidden" or "shown benign" in the blocking sense. The collection-level flag still fires, so the drop is still flagged, just no longer by name.

Why it is not lower: the one summary line a reviewer reads names only the PR's padding. Seeded data loss sits behind "and N more". That is a real hiding gap in the flag summary, which is the medium class. It is not perf, so W28=B does not apply.

Caveats:
- #37's current head e0b635c still renders flags from the older per-field shape. Its flagText shows `users: column dropped, PR 6, base 0` and never reads `fields`. So the panel impact depends on how #37 adopts the new `fields`.
- Keeping declared order alone is weaker than the claim suggests. MySQL `ADD COLUMN … FIRST`, or a migration that rebuilds the table, can reorder columns. The robust fix is the claim's main one: list fields the base pane's snapshot also declares first, or keep them as their own flags.

The mechanics hold and they belong to #35. I lowered the severity from medium to low.

**Setup.** Fresh clone at pr35 = 4a284f9. `git diff --name-status 561bd84..HEAD` lists only #35's files: CHANGELOG.md, README.md, lib/data-diff.mjs, package.json and test/data-diff.test.mjs. The fold is new in 7193877..4a284f9:
- `tally` changed from per-field to `add('column-dropped', null, c.fieldsDropped.length, [...c.fieldsDropped])` (L915);
- `flagChanges` L833 builds `fields: [...mine.items].sort().slice(0, 5)`.

**Reproduced.** Probe: `verify-adversarial-2-scope/probe-colfold.mjs`, output in `out-probe-colfold.txt`. Seeded users has id, email and name. The PR pane's S1 adds the padding, and its Sn keeps only id and name.

| Padding | Flag | 'email' in any flag? |
|---|---|---|
| none (control) | count 1, fields `['email']` | yes |
| 4 `aa_tmp_` | count 5, `email` 5th in `fields` | yes |
| 5 `aa_tmp_` | count 6, fields `aa_tmp_0000`–`0004` | no |
| 1,600 `aa_` | count 1601, fields `aa_0000`–`0004` | no |
| 5 `zz_` | `email` listed first | yes |

In every case the flag is red with `shared` false, trusted or not. The test at test L341-343 asserts "the first five by name, whatever the declared order", so the sort is deliberate. No test drops a seeded column beside padding.

**Why it is not blocking under W28=B:**
- The drop is not hidden. The users column-dropped flag is red, unshared and counted (6 or 1,601). It stays at the top among the base pane's flags. The count is larger than the five names given.
- It is not excused. `shared` uses the full multiset of items, email included, so it can't turn amber unless the base dropped every field too.
- It is not a regression of flagging. At 7193877, email's drop had its own flag. Now the drop is still flagged as part of the collection's flag; only its name moved out of the five-name sample. At 7193877, a padding of 100 or more also pushed email's per-field flag out of #37's 100-flag list, and that design buried other collections' deletes.

**Why low, not medium:**
- The name is still in what #35 hands on. The PR diff's `fieldsDropped` keeps the declared order, so email comes first under Postgres ADD COLUMN, which appends. Divergence has `{kind: 'field-dropped', field: 'email', status: 'pr-only'}`.
- #37's panel (e0b635c) lists "Fields dropped" from that diff in declared order, up to 50. So in the claim's own scenario the reviewer sees "email" first when they open users.
- The earlier burying findings were rated medium because a seeded collection's whole flag left the capped list. Here the flag for that collection and kind stays at index 0. Only which name gets sampled is affected, which is a milder case of the same class.
- #37's current `flagText` doesn't render `fields` or `count` yet (it still reads per-field `field`). So the "reads as a cleanup of the PR's own columns" effect only appears once #37 adopts this engine. The engine's choice of which names to give is still #35's.
- No doc claim is wrong. README L440 and CHANGELOG say "the first five", which the code does. L447's "a PR's padding … can't push a delete out" is still true across flags.

**Worst case.** With MySQL `ADD COLUMN … FIRST` and 50 or more padding columns, email could drop out of #36's 50-item listed fields and the sorted divergence too. Even then the flag "users: column dropped, red, count 1,601+" stays at the top, which nobody would read as benign.

**Fix.** The claim's fix is sound and cheap:
- list first the dropped fields that the base pane's snapshot also declares, with their own count; the reference is already read in `diffSnapshots`;
- at the least, keep the declared order instead of sorting by name;
- add a test with five padding columns that sort before 'email', dropped with it, where 'email' must appear in `fields`.
